summary: Charles DiSimone is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of Munich in 2016. He has held posts at the University of Munich, Buddhist Digital Resource Center, and Ghent University.

Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Burma Research Society. He served as Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1906–1919) and Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology who earned multiple degrees, including a PhD and D.Litt., from the University of London. He taught at SOAS (~1953–1959) and served as Commissioner of Archaeology (1956–1967).

Charles Egbert Kennet (1826–1884) worked in religious studies and Indology, having studied at Bishop's College, Calcutta. He served as Principal of Madras Theological College from 1877 and was a Fellow at the University of Madras (~1877–1884).

Charles Eliot (1862–1931) was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a BA from Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Foreign Office (~1886–1904) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sheffield (~1905–1912) and Hong Kong (1912–1918).

Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist who studied at Fort William College (~1801–1803). He worked for the East India Company (~1795–1826) and served as Treasurer for the Royal Asiatic Society (~1838–1856).

Charles Evelyn Arbuthnot William Oldham (1869–1949) worked in Indology and archaeology after studying at Balliol College, Oxford (~1888–1890). He served as Assistant Editor of Indian Antiquary (~1925–1931) and Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1935–1941).

Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) was a medical scholar and anthropologist who studied at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He taught Bronisław Malinowski and held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Georges Marcel Autran (1879–1952) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale, and later served as a Professor at Aix-Marseille University.
Charles Godfrey Chenevix Trench (1877–1964) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lincoln College, University of Oxford, where he earned a B.A. (~1896–1900).

Charles Goodman is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard. He held a post as Associate Professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar who earned his BD and PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara (~1991–1996).

Charles Hallisey (1953–) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and Chicago. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1987–1991), Harvard (1996–2001, 2007), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2001, 2005).

Charles Hamilton (1752–1792) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He served in the military with the East India Company starting in 1776 and was an early member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1792).

Charles Harris (1859–1943) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington and under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (PhD 1884). He was Professor of German at Oberlin College and Case Western Reserve University.

Charles Henry Allan Bennett (1872–1923) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Buddhasasana Samagama and The Buddhist Review, and served as head of the Buddhist Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1908.

Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1880), held multiple roles at Presidency University, and served as Librarian of the India Office (1893–1903).

Charles Hubert Biddulph (1898–1966) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Philander Smith College and the Crystal Palace School of Engineering. He held various engineering and managerial roles at the South Indian Railway Company from 1924 to 1966.
Charles Hyart (1913–2004) was a linguist who studied at the University of Liège (~1931–1935) under René Fohalle. He later returned to the University of Liège to teach Russian from ~1948 to 1983.

Charles James Lyall (1845–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1867–1898) and as Professor of Arabic at Oxford (1913–1920).
